title: Why JFET Current Goes Flat Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 12
description:
Aarav slowly turns up the supply on a JFET. At first the current climbs like a normal resistor, then it stops climbing: more voltage, same current. Why? We start with a hose that pinches near the far end when you push harder, then look inside the JFET as V_DS pinches the drain end of the channel.

On a live breadboard V_DS sweeps from 0 to 12 V while the drain characteristics plot themselves: the ohmic region, pinch-off at V_P, the flat saturation (constant current) region at I_DSS, and breakdown. Then we repeat for V_GS = -1 V and -2 V, build the transfer characteristic from the flat values and meet Shockley's equation. We define drain resistance r_d, transconductance g_m and amplification factor mu, and prove mu = r_d x g_m step by step. A worked example finds all three, followed by the exam trap (pinch-off does not make the current zero), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 63 of PUC Electronics, Class 12, Chapter 1: Field Effect Transistor (FET) (Karnataka II PUC Electronics). The FET is not in the rationalised NCERT/CBSE Class 12 Physics book or the ISC Physics syllabus, so this lesson follows the Karnataka PUC Electronics syllabus.
